def test_gaussian_norm_bit_bound_with_coprime_denominators(self) -> None:
        module = load(MEDIATOR)
        bits = 4096
        first = 1 << (bits-1)
        second = first+1
        value = module.GaussianRational(Q(1, first), Q(1, second))
        norm = value.norm_sq()
        expected = Q(first*first+second*second, (first*second)**2)
        self.assertEqual(norm, expected)
        self.assertGreater(norm.denominator.bit_length(), 2*bits)
        self.assertLessEqual(norm.numerator.bit_length(), 4*bits+1)
        self.assertLessEqual(norm.denominator.bit_length(), 4*bits)
        self.refused(module.normalized_concurrence_squared, value.re, value.im, kind="resource")
old_cost: Fixed rational operations; each stored component at most 4096 bits, norm may use twice that width.
corrected_cost: Fixed exact rational operations on components with numerator/denominator at most B=4096 bits. For re=a/b and im=c/d, norm=(a^2*d^2+c^2*b^2)/(b^2*d^2): numerator at most4B+1 bits, denominator at most4B bits. The norm return is not itself gated to B bits. Inverse intermediates have at most5B+1 bits before result-component admission. Returned Gaussian components are always admitted to B bits; no iterative unbounded algebra.
derivation: Each |a|,b,|c|,d<2^B. Each squared numerator term is <2^(4B), their sum <2^(4B+1), denominator <2^(4B); reduction cannot increase either. With b=2^4095 and d=b+1, the reduced norm denominator has16381 bits, disproving the previous8192-bit ceiling. The exact implementation is unchanged. The concurrence API rejects this oversized derived norm with a resource Failure.
